questions.question: What is the core principle of saving?
options: Deciding to set aside a portion of your money for later
Waiting for someone to give you money for getting good grades
Buying as many items as possible on sale to technically "save"
Exchanging small coins for paper banknotes at a local bank
questions.explanation: Saving is fundamentally about making a conscious decision to set aside money for future use rather than spending it immediately.

questions.question: Where is it appropriate to keep your saved money?
options: Only with parents, because children are not allowed to have their own money
Money should not be kept anywhere; it must always stay in circulation
At home in a piggy bank or in a bank account
In a commercial bank, as saving at home is not safe or trustworthy
questions.explanation: Saved money can be kept safely in a piggy bank at home for everyday savings or in a bank account for larger amounts.

questions.question: Do small amounts matter when saving?
options: They only matter if you deposit them in a bank to earn interest
Yes, with regular saving, they gradually add up
No, small coins have too little value to ever change anything
Yes, but only if you save them once a year in one large sum
questions.explanation: Regular saving of small amounts is very effective because they accumulate over time into a significant sum.

questions.question: Every week, Chrumko puts one coin into his piggy bank. What will he notice over time?
options: That the coins in the piggy bank multiplied all by themselves
That thanks to consistency, he has enough for something more expensive
That the piggy bank is still as light as it was at the beginning
That the money in the piggy bank has expired and is no longer valid
questions.explanation: Through consistent weekly saving, even small amounts accumulate to create enough money for more expensive purchases.

questions.question: Chrumko's toy broke, and he immediately buys a new one using his savings. Why?
options: He was lucky and found money on the street in front of the shop
He had created a reserve for unexpected expenses
The toy store gave him a new toy for free as a special gift
His parents were legally required to pay the remaining balance
questions.explanation: By maintaining savings, Chrumko had a financial cushion available for unexpected situations like replacing a broken toy.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of having saved money?
options: More space in your wallet for photos and loyalty cards
The certainty that prices in shops will never rise again
The ability to brag to friends about having a high balance
Greater freedom in your future decision-making
questions.explanation: Savings give you the flexibility to make future purchases and decisions without being dependent on others or immediate income.

questions.question: What happens if we spend all our money as soon as we get it?
options: Shops will automatically send us bonus money for spending
Later, we will lack money for more important things
We will have twice as much money in the near future
Parents are required by law to give us extra pocket money
questions.explanation: Spending all money immediately means we won't have resources available when we face more important or urgent needs later.

questions.question: Why is it better to have savings than to always ask others for money?
options: Because asking others for money is strictly forbidden by law
Savings give us independence to buy what we want
If we save by ourselves, the coins in the piggy bank shine brighter
Asking for money takes longer than taking it from a piggy bank
questions.explanation: Having savings provides independence and allows us to make our own choices without relying on others for financial help.

questions.question: Chrumko sees a book in the bookstore that costs more than his weekly allowance. What does he do?
options: He borrows money from a stranger standing in line
He uses his previous savings
He has to wait until the shop declares the book as trash
He simply can never afford to buy the book
questions.explanation: By having accumulated savings, Chrumko can purchase items that cost more than his regular weekly allowance.

questions.question: Why doesn't Chrumko have to wait "a very long time" to buy a more expensive item?
options: Because he ran to the shop faster than all the other customers
Because he was building up savings over time
Because the bank canceled half the price from his account
Because he only buys things that are damaged and cheap
questions.explanation: By consistently building up savings over time, Chrumko can afford expensive items much sooner than if he had no savings.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a short-term and a long-term goal?
options: A long-term goal requires more time and patience
A short-term goal always costs more than a thousand euros
A short-term goal can only be purchased during weekends
In practice, there is no real difference between these goals
questions.explanation: Long-term goals require extended periods of saving and sustained effort, while short-term goals can be achieved quickly.

questions.question: What is needed to achieve a long-term goal?
options: To completely stop spending on food and school supplies
Patience and regular saving
Lots of luck in finding lost coins on the ground
Spending all savings on random things every Monday
questions.explanation: Long-term goals require consistent saving habits and patience to maintain regular contributions over an extended period.

questions.question: Chrumko wants to buy stickers (cheap) and a building set (expensive). How does he solve this?
options: He saves for both goals at the same time
He buys the stickers and decides to steal the building set instead
He buys the building set immediately, even though he lacks the money
He decides not to save and throws his money away right now
questions.explanation: By saving for multiple goals simultaneously, Chrumko can work towards both the short-term goal (stickers) and long-term goal (building set).

questions.question: Chrumko has been saving for a building set for 10 weeks. What category does this goal fall into?
options: An immediate purchase without any waiting
A short-term goal (lasting only one day)
An unreachable goal for any child
A long-term goal (requires more time)
questions.explanation: A goal that takes 10 weeks of consistent saving is considered a long-term goal because it requires sustained effort over an extended period.

questions.question: Chrumko found out that the building set (long-term goal) is on sale. What does he do if he has only saved half?
options: He buys half of the building set and leaves the rest in the shop
He must continue saving until he has the full amount
He cries in the middle of the shop so they give it to him for free
He spends the money on 100 stickers instead so nothing is left
questions.explanation: Even with a sale, Chrumko needs to continue saving to afford the complete building set, as his current savings only cover half.

questions.question: What is a "financial reserve"?
options: Money set aside specifically for a birthday party
A list of toys that Chrumko plans to buy in the summer
Money for unexpected needs
Money we accidentally forgot in the pocket of old pants
questions.explanation: A financial reserve is a pool of money set aside to handle unforeseen expenses and emergencies.

questions.question: Does a reserve always have to have a pre-determined purpose (e.g., for a new phone)?
options: Yes, because money without a label spoils quickly in a wallet
No, the reserve serves for unexpected expenses
Yes, because without an intention, we easily spend it on useless things
A reserve is only created when we have an excess of coins
questions.explanation: A reserve is specifically meant to be flexible and available for any unexpected need, not tied to a specific purchase.

questions.question: Chrumko has a reserve in an envelope. At school, he finds out he needs materials for a project. What does he do?
options: He must borrow money from a teacher or the principal
He uses his reserve and buys the materials
He doesn't submit the project and automatically gets a failing grade
He goes to the bank to apply for a student loan
questions.explanation: This is exactly what a reserve is for—using it to handle unexpected expenses like the school project materials.

questions.question: What does the fact that he has a reserve bring to Chrumko?
options: Fear that someone will swap his envelope money at night
A sense of security in everyday life
Sadness because he can never actually use that money
Boredom, because you can't have any fun with a reserve
questions.explanation: Having a financial reserve provides peace of mind and security, knowing that resources are available for unexpected situations.

questions.question: Can Chrumko use his reserve for ice cream when he passes a stand?
options: Yes, if he feels like having ice cream and doesn't need the money
He can, but it wouldn't be very wise
No, the reserve technically cannot be taken out of the envelope
Only if he buys ice cream for all of his classmates as well
questions.explanation: While technically he could use the reserve for ice cream, it would defeat the purpose of having an emergency fund available for real needs.

questions.question: What is key when saving from small amounts?
options: Finding the largest possible piggy bank so the coins get lost inside
Setting aside a huge sum of money only once every ten years
Doing it repeatedly and regularly
Only saving coins that we believe bring us good luck
questions.explanation: The key to successful saving is consistency and regularity, not the size of each individual amount.

questions.question: What happens to small coins after a long period of saving?
options: There will still be as few of them as on the first day
They turn into a larger sum
The coins in the piggy bank fade over time and lose their value
They will take up too much space, so it's not worth storing them
questions.explanation: Through consistent accumulation, small coins combine to form a significantly larger amount over time.

questions.question: Chrumko saves 50 cents a week and it seems like very little to him. What would you advise him?
options: To stop, because 50 cents doesn't mean anything
To give the money to the first person he sees on the street
To keep going, he will see the result later
To ask older classmates for money instead
questions.explanation: 50 cents per week adds up to €26 per year—a substantial amount that demonstrates the power of consistent small savings.

questions.question: Chrumko bought an item that one small portion of money wouldn't cover. How is this possible?
options: The shopkeeper made a mistake in his favor at the checkout
Regular saving added up the small amounts
He found the remaining money hidden under a pillow in his room
The money in the piggy bank miraculously doubled overnight
questions.explanation: By saving regularly, even small amounts accumulate to sufficient funds to purchase items that individual small payments couldn't cover.

questions.question: What would happen if Chrumko only saved 50 cents when he was in a "good mood"?
options: He would save much more because a good mood attracts money
The amount would grow unpredictably and take much longer
The bank would cancel all his savings due to inconsistency
The coins in the piggy bank would start to smell because they were alone for so long
questions.explanation: Without consistency, savings become irregular and unpredictable, taking much longer to accumulate to meaningful amounts.
